candidates.reason: Workable three-column banner: the headline is dominant and the CTA is clear. Flaws: the logo is shrunk to a tiny circle and the QUILLBROOK wordmark can't be read. The body copy is squeezed into a narrow 7-line ragged column ("Chocolate," sits alone on a line) set almost as heavy as the headline, so the two compete. The NEW HARVEST pill is oversized next to the shrunken logo, and the medallion is cramped against the right edge.

Nearly the same as candidate 1, with slightly better body wrapping (6 lines). Flaws: the logo is even smaller and its wordmark can't be read. The body copy is still a heavy narrow column competing with the headline. The fine print wraps awkwardly, leaving "to order" alone on its own line. The medallion is squeezed into the right corner and the badge pill is larger than the logo.

Logo and medallion are kept intact and in proportion, but the grouping is broken. The CTA floats mid-canvas, cut off from its body copy and headline column. The body copy is jammed against the bottom-left edge with almost no margin. The NEW HARVEST badge drifts on its own against the medallion's halo, and the fine print hangs loose under the button. The reading order and alignment feel arbitrary.

This is the square original shrunk and centred, not a redesign. The body copy, CTA label and fine print are microscopic and can't be read, and the logo and badge are tiny. Large empty bands on the left and right waste the banner format.
